why: Settlement compile warnings that are named, owned and tracked rather than silently tolerated. The exporter still refuses to publish on any UNEXPLAINED warning: a warning outside this register is a hard error; so is a register row that has started passing; so is a row whose place is not in the compiled set. Each row names the owner and where the work is queued, so a row can never become a quiet holding position. Keys are (placeId, subjectId, ruleId) taken from the compiled floodBandReport's structured rows, so a row survives a change in the measured sample counts and dies when the finding itself dies.
